guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.whole: All 18 participating villages submitted conservation goals to planning authorities and 26,900 people were given access to improved sanitation, both targets met, and the project renovated 1,040 traditional houses against 1,225 planned at appraisal and a target cut to 823 at the 2014 restructuring. It trained 3,215 people in traditional and tourism-related skills, with 290 trained in intangible heritage against a target of 250, improved 69 kilometres of access roads and paths, and improved the facilities at three natural heritage sites. Annual tourist visits to the key project sites reached 4.08 million at loan closing against a target of 4.36 million that was never changed, and the completion report records 4.49 million by 15 September 2017, three months after closing; it says the visits at closing were likely held down by heavier than normal seasonal rain in 2016 at the Shanmu River Scenic Park, which is known for rafting. Visitors to the gateway town information centres at Jianhe, Leishan and Liping came to 4,800 against a revised target of 4,500 and an appraisal target of 8,500, the fourth centre in Guiyang having been dropped during restructuring. Other works were cut at the July 2014 restructuring: the museum for the Dingxiao National Geo-Park, for want of a feasible design, the Provincial Tourist Information and Service Centre, for want of suitable land, and the number of demonstration houses, from 77 to 34; the Independent Evaluation Group's review puts the cost removed by the museum's cancellation and the reduced scope of the cultural heritage component at about US$2.36 million. Average income at project sites rose from RMB 3,160 a person in 2010 to RMB 6,131 in 2016, employment in tourism and hospitality at those sites from 3,023 people in 2010 to 13,551 in 2016, and in five project areas the number of people counted as poor fell from 18,181 in 2010, when the poverty line was RMB 650 a person a year, to 14,735 in 2016, when it was RMB 3,160. The report says the project's own share in these changes cannot be established: it produced no tracer studies of the people it trained, did not track the residence or ethnicity of those who gained from tourism, and records tourist numbers across Guizhou growing 24 per cent a year from 2011 to 2015. Economic rates of return recalculated for four sample sites at completion were 17.8 per cent at Wanfenglin and 19.1 per cent at Jiuzhou, both above their appraisal figures, and 17.5 per cent at Langde and 12.4 per cent at Zhaoxing, both below; the appraisal figures are 13.7, 10.2, 19.6 and 12.6 per cent in the report's table, while the report's own text and the review summarise them as a range from 13.7 to 19.6 per cent and label 13.7 as Jiuzhou, which the table gives as 10.2. Both the report and the review rate efficiency Substantial. Final cost was US$94.85 million including interest during construction, about 105.6 per cent of the US$89.84 million estimated at appraisal. All these figures are the lender's own, from its completion report and the Evaluation Group's review of it; the Group sits inside the World Bank Group, and no check from outside it was found.
guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.why: Checked against ICR00004154 and ICRR0021065 in full for the sections used. Corrections: the review's efficiency section attributes the US$2.36 million to the July 2014 reduction in the scope of several Component 1 activities together with the dropping of the Dingxiao museum, not to the museum and the Provincial Tourist Information and Service Centre; the demonstration houses cut from 77 to 34 (review, component 1 description) was missing; the rain explanation is the report's own hedge ('it is likely', footnote 2) and is now given as such; the EIRR label conflict is stated with the table's own figure for Jiuzhou. Framework rows all verified; the only adverse rows are tourist visits and houses renovated against the original target, both present. ICR paragraph 1003 says no project-level financial rate of return was needed, so no FIRR claim is made.

kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.whole: The project built Line 3's 38.2 kilometres of track and all 17 of its stations, both targets met, and the line opened in August 2017. The track, station, on-time performance, user satisfaction and floor-area-ratio indicators were all created at the March 2015 restructuring. Average weekday ridership after six months of operation was 153,800, against 200,000 at appraisal and a target cut to 150,000 at that restructuring. Peak-period travel time between two origin and destination pairs on the corridor fell from 43 minutes to 14 and from 38 minutes to 15, against targets of 22.5 and 17.5; on-time performance was 99 per cent against a target of 98, user satisfaction 91.2 per cent against 80, and the floor area ratio of new development along the line 1.6 times the surrounding district's against a target above 1. The satisfaction figure comes from surveys run by an outside party but paid for out of the project. Thirteen of the 17 stations had bus or bicycle facilities within 50 metres of an exit, which the completion report puts at 76 per cent of its target, and four of the 17 interchange works were delayed, with their road construction and pavements unfinished at closing, which the Evaluation Group's review attributes to lower passenger demand than expected. The restructuring of bus routes to feed the metro was recorded as only partly achieved: an integrated fare card was in use and 12 new feeder routes were introduced, but the review, citing the report, says it may take up to three years before all the feeder routes are operating, which cuts the rate of return by 0.2 percentage points. Six indicators were dropped at the March 2015 restructuring, among them the ridership and revenue attributable to Line 3, the rail company's working ratio, and the share of new development occurring along rail lines. The transit-oriented development proposed in 2013 and 2014 above the Shizui depot was cancelled in 2015, which the report attributes to changes in national land administration policy and a change of city leadership, and the design reverted to the depot as approved; property developments around the eastern stations at Dashuying, Jinmasi, Taipingcun and Hongqiao were postponed, which the report attributes to unfavourable real estate market conditions. The report puts the economic rate of return at 7.9 per cent over a 30-year period, covering 99 per cent of project cost, against an appraisal figure its own table gives as 8.5 per cent and the review reads from the appraisal document as 8.0 per cent. The report's paragraph 44 gives relevance High and efficacy and efficiency Substantial; the review rates efficiency Substantial, noting the project was 19 months late partly because Kunming delayed the start of construction while three metro lines were being built at once and partly because of household relocation, and adding that complex metro projects can now be supported at much lower rates of return than at appraisal because benefits such as access to jobs and land values are counted. Spending came to US$1,803.9 million against US$1,711.6 million estimated at appraisal, with the US$300 million loan revised to US$276.9 million and that amount disbursed. All these figures are the lender's own; no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.why: Checked against ICR00004604 (Annex 1 including the full version with deleted indicators, paragraphs 32-44 and Table 2) and ICRR0021559 in full. Corrections: the rows for track, stations, on-time performance, user satisfaction and floor area ratio are marked 'New' in the full annex, so their targets were set at the 2015 restructuring; the user satisfaction survey is described in the dropped-indicator comment as 'surveys conducted by an independent party, funded though the project', which makes it a fourth project-funded survey in this batch; the Shizui cancellation is attributed in paragraph 35 to national land policy changes and a change of leadership in 2015, and the eastern-end developments were postponed, not cancelled, on unfavourable market conditions, with the four stations named (Jinmasi among them); the feeder-route statement is the review's reading of ICR page 18. Six dropped indicators counted in the annex. Neither document gives a financial rate of return.

hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.whole: By the completion report's count the project built 91.96 kilometres of road against 136.94 planned at appraisal and a target cut to 119 at the December 2015 restructuring, 43.08 kilometres of that in Gansu against a revised 83.20, and rehabilitated 20.37 kilometres against 20.94 at appraisal and a revised 18.60. It gave 134,279 people piped water against 79,665 at appraisal and a revised 89,000 and made 20,123 new household connections against 9,120 and a revised 12,300, though in Gansu only 2,580 connections were made against a revised 5,000; 554,080 people were counted as benefiting from the new and rehabilitated roads, against 540,400 at appraisal and a revised 640,000, and in Hunan that figure was 37,386 against 13,900 at appraisal and a revised 150,000. Hunan is where the zeros sit: no one was recorded as gaining access to water or solid waste management services against 15,900 at appraisal and a revised 10,500, no users of the integrated centres, markets and irrigation facilities against 11,341 and a revised 15,000, no market sales revenue and no market vendors against revised targets of RMB 55 million and 430 vendors, no irrigation improved against 120 hectares at appraisal and a revised target of zero, and no farmer organisations against five at appraisal and a revised target of zero. The reason is in the report's own account: the wastewater treatment plant at Yueshan was finished just before closing and was not in use, against a target of 10,500 beneficiaries, and the farmers' market at Yueshan and the market and service centre at Dingziwan were both built and neither was in use by closing. One town that was to build a farmers' market was dropped from the project and the results framework was not updated to match. Across the three provinces 17 new markets, industrial centres and vocational training centres were built against 23 at appraisal and a revised 18, irrigation was improved on 4,874 hectares against 5,690 and a revised 5,840, 1,226 market vendors were recorded against 3,265 and a revised 2,954, 52,076 people were trained against 40,421 and a revised 62,000 - 2,425 of them in Hunan against a revised 10,000 - 35 studies were completed against 22 and a revised 26, and 1,789 project office staff were trained against 1,352 and a revised 1,340. Project-wide, 79,899 people were recorded using the integrated centres, markets and irrigation facilities against a revised target of 83,000, and 87,470 gained access to water or solid waste management services against 99,900 at appraisal. As of June 2019 the Yueshan plant was in testing mode at a third of its 3,000 cubic metre design capacity, serving 5,000 people, with unit treatment costs risen, subsidies from higher-level government paying for it and no wastewater fee collected, and the report says the markets at Yueshan and Dingziwan had still not attracted enough vendors. Of the 28 towns at appraisal, four were dropped at the 2015 restructuring - Fuxing and Dongli in Guangdong, Zhentou in Hunan and Wenfeng in Gansu, the last because of unresolved land and resettlement problems - with Xiantang added, leaving 25. The national programme for small towns that the project was to be designed and carried out with was cancelled during preparation, which the report says partly explains the shortage of counterpart funding; the project was downgraded to problem status in June 2014 and never left it. The report gives economic rates of return recalculated at completion of 9 to 16 per cent for roads in Hunan, where none was calculated at appraisal, 12.1 per cent for roads in Gansu against 10 to 15 per cent at appraisal, 26 per cent for irrigation in Gansu against 14 to 22 per cent, and 14.4 per cent for Gansu's agricultural markets, for which no appraisal figure existed; both the report and the Evaluation Group's review rate efficiency Substantial and the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, the review rating relevance of objectives Substantial where the report rates it High. Total cost fell from US$296.64 million at appraisal to US$213.18 million, and US$1,571,787.65 of the three loans, about 1 per cent, was cancelled at closing. The beneficiary satisfaction figure of 82 per cent against a 75 per cent target comes from a social and economic impact survey agreed as a remedial measure under the project; every other figure here is the lender's own, and no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.why: Checked against ICR00004709 (Annex 1 row by row including every provincial sub-row, paragraphs 14-18, 26-39, 63-72, 105-114, Annex 7 footnotes 33 and 39-42) and ICRR0021894. Corrections from the shortfall test: Hunan irrigation 0 ha against 120 at appraisal with the target cut to zero, Hunan trainees 2,425 against a revised 10,000, Gansu household connections 2,580 against a revised 5,000, project-wide integrated-centre users 79,899 against a revised 83,000 and water/solid-waste access 87,470 against 99,900 at appraisal were all missing. Paragraphs 37 and 38 were softened: the plant 'was completed just before the project closing date and was not in use, in sharp contrast to its target of 10,500 beneficiaries', and both market buildings 'were completed, but neither building was in use by loan closing, resulting in 0 beneficiaries for PO-4'; paragraph 113 carries the one-third capacity, rising unit costs, subsidies and uncollected fee. Wenfeng's reason is paragraph 15. The pipeline rows are labelled Meter(m) while their values can only be kilometres, so they are still not used; Annex 7 footnotes 39-42 record that several revised town-level targets in the restructuring paper were themselves errors.

wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.whole: By the completion report's count six hospitals were built, renovated or equipped against eight at appraisal and a target cut to six at the June 2020 restructuring, and all eight project hospitals got a standardised cost accounting system producing quarterly departmental unit costs, telemedicine for tele-diagnosis and a place in an annual performance assessment report. The share of inpatients referred up to higher-level hospitals fell from 8.5 per cent to 4.4, against a target tightened from 6 to 5 per cent at the 2017 restructuring, and the average length of stay fell from 10.6 days to 7.5 against a target tightened from 8.5 to 8 days. Twenty high-volume conditions were treated using clinical pathways against 10 at appraisal and a revised 16, the companion measure of the share of admissions treated that way having been dropped; 98 community and township health centres signed referral agreements against 5 at appraisal and a revised 42; 1,863 health staff were trained against a target of 1,400 that was set only at the 2017 restructuring; 637 trainees finished courses with a certificate against 600; and six evaluations of pre-reform packages were done against three at appraisal and a revised one. Outpatient visits at the eight hospitals rose from 1.62 million in 2012 to 2.80 million in 2019 and inpatient admissions from 120,600 to 201,600, figures the report calls additional indicators outside the results framework, and patient satisfaction was 92.85 per cent against a 90 per cent target, on an indicator added in 2020 and measured only in 2019 and 2020. The scope was cut as Wushan's and Qianjiang's hospitals left the loan: Qianjiang county withdrew after securing domestic finance and returned US$13.97 million, Wushan county returned US$4.71 million after the landslide stopped its hospital, US$10 million was cancelled at the October 2019 restructuring and US$8.68 million was moved to three other hospitals. The report says the Bank had put about US$5 million into the Wushan traditional Chinese medicine hospital by the time of the landslide and that this investment has had no return so far and may not have any return in the future. No economic or financial rate of return was calculated at appraisal or at completion; the report's partial analysis puts the net benefit at about RMB 314 million (US$48 million) against a project cost of about RMB 555 million, and both the report and the Evaluation Group's review rate efficiency Modest, on 41 months of extension, 8.5 years from Board approval to closing, and a disbursement rate under 10 per cent in the first four years and 27 per cent near the end of the fifth. Spending came to US$140.8 million against US$155.5 million estimated at appraisal. All these figures are the lender's own; no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.why: Checked against ICR00005207 (Annex 1 row by row, paragraphs 16-28 and 40-45) and ICRR0022804 in full. Every framework row is met or exceeded, so the shortfall test found nothing to add; the only correction is the dropped companion measure on the share of admissions using clinical pathways, recorded in that row's comment. The review's rate-of-return table records no rate available at appraisal and at the ICR, and the report calculates none, so 'none was calculated' stands rather than 'not recalculated'. Figures for the restructurings, the US$5 million with no return, the partial analysis and the disbursement rates all verified in the two documents.

xuancheng-industry-zone-house-demolition.whole: The project built 52 kilometres of non-rural road with storm-water drains, water supply and sewers against 65 planned at appraisal and a target cut to 50 at the 2018 restructuring, and a wastewater treatment plant with its collection network. By the completion report's count net employment in the zone reached 6,449 jobs against 32,000 at appraisal and a revised target of 5,700, incremental value added RMB 1,090 million against 2,300 million at appraisal and a revised 990 million, and 215 firms were attracted against 220 at appraisal and a revised 200; women were 26 per cent of the new jobs against 18 per cent at appraisal and a revised 25 per cent. 18,813 people were given improved water sources and improved sanitation against 80,000 at appraisal and a revised 18,000; the plant treated 9,000 cubic metres a day to Class 1A standard against 17,500 at appraisal and a revised 3,000; and wastewater treatment covered the whole project area against an 80 per cent target set in 2018. One row fell short on its own terms: 35.6 tonnes a year of biochemical oxygen demand were removed against 1,213 tonnes at appraisal and a revised 153 tonnes, which the report attributes to less sewage reaching the plant than expected and to the zone administration's own environmental standards for the firms in the park, leaving the collected wastewater much less polluted than assumed. An intelligent investment promotion system, a labour market information system, an internal monitoring system covering more than 300 companies and a real-time environmental monitoring system were all delivered. The project area was cut from 20.2 to 14.6 square kilometres at the January 2017 restructuring, cancelling ten roads with their underground networks and one overpass, and the loan was cut at the same time from US$150 million to US$90 million, with the disbursement share for civil works raised from 61 to 100 per cent; five more roads were cancelled later. Land acquired came to 1,984.15 mu against 2,558.1 mu in the resettlement plan, or 2,169.21 mu once the five cancelled roads are left out, and the houses of 86 households were demolished against 161 planned. The report puts the economic rate of return at completion at 6.8 per cent counting employment and wages and 14.7 per cent counting total value added, against 10.4 and 32.7 per cent at appraisal, and attributes the fall to the longer development period and less commercial development than expected; both the report and the Evaluation Group's review rate efficiency Substantial, the review's table giving 32.7 per cent at appraisal and 14.7 per cent at completion over 97.9 and 97.1 per cent of project cost. The report also records savings of US$4.6 million in mid-2018, from bidding below estimate and from land acquisition and resettlement costing less than planned, spent on extra water quality monitoring equipment, 22 contracts of which only a few overran, and tenders often drawing 30 to 40 bids. Spending came to US$168.9 million against US$343.6 million estimated at appraisal, with US$87.3 million of the loan disbursed. The satisfaction figure of 74.2 per cent against a 70 per cent target is the third of four surveys run under the project, in December 2019; the fourth, in June 2020, gave 72 per cent, each round covered 240 to 380 people, and the report says the results among firms and vendors should be treated as indicative only. Every other figure here is the lender's own, and no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
xuancheng-industry-zone-house-demolition.why: Checked against ICR00005221 (Annex 1 row by row, paragraphs 15-21, 61-65, Annex 7 paragraphs 8-10 and the survey annex) and ICRR0022533 including its rate table. Corrections: the 74.2 per cent is Survey 3's figure (Annex 7 records satisfaction of 63.6, 67.4 and 74.2 per cent in the first three rounds and a fall 'between Survey 3 and Survey 4, from 74 to 72 percent', with the sample sizes and the 'indicative only' caveat); paragraph 64 attributes the US$4.6 million of savings to successful bidding and to lower-than-planned land acquisition and resettlement costs; Annex 7 paragraph 8 gives 2,169.21 mu as the comparable plan figure once the cancelled roads are excluded, and paragraph 9 gives 86 households demolished against 161 planned. All other framework rows verified; the only short row is BOD removed, which was already present.

moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.whole: By the completion report's count the project rehabilitated 218 kilometres of non-rural road in Sichuan against a target of 200 and 36.1 kilometres in Gansu against 35.9, restored traffic to pre-earthquake levels on all project roads, and supported 14 water utilities in Sichuan - six wastewater plants and eight water treatment plants, with 116.5 kilometres of water supply pipe, 442.9 kilometres of sewage and drainage pipe and four booster pumping stations - and five in Gansu, with three wastewater plants, two water plants, 62.8 kilometres of water supply pipe and 109.2 kilometres of sewers. It built, renovated or equipped 60 health facilities in Sichuan and seven in Gansu and 186 classrooms in Gansu; beds in Sichuan's project facilities rose from 3,221 before the earthquake to 5,374, and the report puts the population served by Sichuan's health works at 9.82 million. Seven of the rows - the road, utility, health facility and classroom counts - are Bank-wide core indicators added in June 2014, six of them with no appraisal target at all. One row fell short: half of Gansu's county towns were recorded as having water supply restored at least to pre-earthquake levels against a target of all of them, because the Cheng county water treatment plant had not been completed or connected and was expected to operate in June 2017, once the Moba Gorge reservoir had been filled. Twenty-nine of Gansu's 31 subprojects were completed; the two left were the Moba Gorge dam and that water plant, which were 23 months late and which the report puts at about US$31 million between them and the Evaluation Group's review at US$38.93 million, or 32 per cent of the cost of Gansu's infrastructure recovery programme. Primary schools were dropped from the project and paid for under China's own earthquake recovery programme, and the review records that resettlement problems delayed roads in Wuhu district and Cheng county and that some roads were dropped or realigned to reduce the resettlement needed. In Sichuan, loan savings of about US$41 million together with extra counterpart funds paid for a third batch of works, all of which were finished except one small road. No economic analysis was done at appraisal, because the loan was an emergency operation, and none was done at completion: the report assessed cost effectiveness, service restoration and local economic recovery instead, and says the savings to local governments from more resilient infrastructure after the 2013 Lushan earthquake could not be quantified. The completion report rates efficiency Substantial and the outcome Satisfactory; the review rates efficiency Modest, capacity building in Gansu Modest and the outcome Moderately Satisfactory. Of the US$710 million loan, US$695.80 million was disbursed. All these figures are the lender's own; no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.why: Checked against ICR00003783 (section F, all 14 PDO and 10 intermediate rows, paragraphs 79-88, Annex 3 paragraph 1) and ICRR0020667 in full. Corrections: seven rows carry the asterisk for Bank-wide core indicators added in June 2014, not six, and six of those show no appraisal target while the Sichuan roads row shows 0; the 9.82 million people served is Sichuan's figure (paragraph 83); the review's own figures are US$38.93 million for the dam and water plant and 32 per cent of the total infrastructure recovery programme of Gansu, against about US$31 million in the report, so both are given with their sources; 'Twenty nine of the 31 subprojects were completed' is the review's own count. The review's rate table is empty at appraisal and at the ICR, which supports the statement that no rate was ever calculated.

zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.whole: The Guangrun component's two stations have a combined installed capacity of 28.4 MW, and the carbon finance completion report records generation at about half what was expected. Against an appraisal figure of 95.66 GWh a year, output was 11.44 GWh in 2010, 11.77 in 2011, 11.80 in 2012, 26.51 in 2013, 46.27 in 2014, 36.22 in 2015, 46.39 in 2016, 53.00 in 2017 - its best year, at 55 per cent of the design figure - 33.00 in 2018 and 16 in 2019. Certified emission reductions contracted under the purchase agreement were cut from 485,000 to 249,590 and then to 157,745 because generation fell, and 145,699 were delivered: 92 per cent of the amended contract and, the report says, 30 per cent of the original feasibility estimate. For the last monitoring period, March 2014 to June 2016, the report's data sheet gives delivery of 94,924 against 104,970 contracted while its own Table 4 gives 92,924, and only the lower figure adds up to the 145,699 total. The component overran its 2006 appraisal estimate by 90 per cent, a cost overrun of US$32.86 million, which the report attributes to unexpected geological conditions, higher prices for labour and raw materials, higher interest during construction and the cost of resettlement, most of it incurred after the Bank loan closed in 2011. Construction was still unfinished in December 2019: a decision on the right bank slope treatment and the crest spillway sluice gates at Zhamushui had not been taken, and two water diversion tunnels and the second-stage treatment of the Hongwawu reservoir's right bank were suspended pending two water allocation disputes with a neighbouring province. All of the county town's drinking water comes from the Zhamushui reservoir at an agreed charge of 0.41 yuan a cubic metre, about 12 million yuan a year, which the report's footnote says the county government never paid; the project company stopped paying the Bank loan and interest in 2013, about 8 million yuan a year, and the county government paid instead, more than 30 million yuan by early 2019. An advance payment of US$388,000 against the carbon credits funded a community benefit plan in the nine villages affected, finished in early 2011 with an acceptance report in May 2011, and 20 per cent of the component's value added tax went to the Jianshi county poverty alleviation fund for the six years 2012 to 2017; the report puts the rise in income of the people directly affected at about 18.37 per cent against 2007, and lists among the project's benefits improved flood control and water supply for more than 70,000 people in Jianshi county and more than 1,500 construction jobs with 60 permanent posts. The financial rate of return on total investment was 5.44 per cent at appraisal without carbon revenue and 7 per cent with it, against a benchmark of 8 per cent, and at completion is below zero, about minus 3.12 per cent, with income half the appraisal figure and investment twice it. The economic rate of return for Guangrun in the 2020 report is minus 0.6 per cent excluding emission benefits, 0.0 per cent with local emission benefits and 2.7 per cent with local and global benefits, against 2.7, 4.2 and 9.1 per cent for the same component at the 2012 completion report and 9.5, 11.0 and 16.0 per cent there for the five-component project as a whole. The report rates the loan project's relevance High, efficacy Modest, efficiency Negligible and outcome Unsatisfactory, and the carbon finance operation's relevance High, efficacy Substantial, efficiency Modest and outcome Moderately Satisfactory; it records that the owner, Guodian, has classified the project as a negative asset and was negotiating to sell it back to the Jianshi county government. All these figures are the lender's own, from the Bank's completion report on the carbon finance operation; no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.why: Checked against report 153668 (P094795_ICR) in full through paragraph 44, including the data sheet's Table 1, Table 1 of generation by year, Table 4 of contracted and generated CERs and Tables 2 and 3 of rates. Corrections: the two tables give different figures for the third monitoring period (94,924 in the data sheet, 92,924 in Table 4) and only the latter reconciles with the 145,699 total, so both are given; paragraph 52 adds that the delivered total is 92 per cent of the amended contract and 30 per cent of the initial feasibility estimate; the 9.5/11.0/16.0 per cent figures for the whole project sit in the 'ICR at 2012' column of Table 3, so they are dated; paragraph 40 gives the carbon finance operation's full set of ratings, including efficiency Modest. Noted but not used: the heading of section 2.2 calls the loan project's achievement of outcomes Moderately Unsatisfactory while paragraphs 35 and 39 and the ratings table give Unsatisfactory.

wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.whole: No completion report for this project has been published; the Evaluation Group's review of it is the only evaluative document, and every figure here reaches the reader through that review. It reports that the project carried out 41 schemes - 26 road segments, four interchanges and 11 pedestrian facilities - and added an 8.2 kilometre connection from the Sanjintan interchange to the fourth Yangtze rail bridge, which could not be provided for at appraisal because the bridge's location had not been settled. Travel time was measured at three locations: at the first the target was reached exactly, an improvement of five minutes over the baseline; at the second there was a saving of one minute, five minutes better than the baseline; at the third the result was three minutes under target, which the review attributes to continuing peak-hour congestion on a bridge over the Han river. Average daily bus ridership rose from 2.59 million person trips in 2002 to 4.54 million against a target of 3.10 million, while Wuhan's travel demand grew 70 per cent between 2002 and 2009 and the public transport share of trips stayed at about 23 to 24 per cent. The vehicle emission control strategy and a new vehicle inspection facility were completed as planned; the road maintenance management system was installed three years late and its data were still being collected at closing, so it could not yet produce the annual maintenance plans intended at appraisal. The third sub-objective, reform of bus service delivery, is rated Negligible: the technical assistance study was completed to the Bank's satisfaction, but Wuhan decided to keep public transport within government rather than tender bus routes competitively, which was the indicator for that sub-objective. Works were dropped along the way: four roads and two interchanges, as not yet needed at the traffic volumes seen; eight of eleven passenger interchanges and five of twelve terminals, over low user volumes, land acquisition problems and timing; a pedestrianised street, because no agreement could be reached on the site; and three bus priority lanes, because of construction works on the routes. In all, the review says the city's public transport company failed to implement 13 of 37 public transport infrastructure subprojects. Eight safety enhancement corridors were added, some blackspot sites having already been treated with local funds. The review gives US$398.20 million and US$1,110.66 million as the project's cost at appraisal and at completion in its data sheet, and the same two figures as the borrower's contribution, up 279 per cent, in its text, where it says the cost net of the front-end fee rose by US$713 million, the first of the five reasons listed being a US$321 million increase in the cost of resettlement. All but US$1 million of the US$200 million loan was disbursed and the closing date was extended by one year, in part because of delays in resettlement. The review puts the economic rate of return at 21.4 per cent at completion covering 94 per cent of project cost, against 23 per cent at appraisal covering 93 per cent, at a 12 per cent discount rate, and rates efficiency Substantial. It rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory against the completion report's Satisfactory and Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory against the report's Satisfactory, and records that the Bank's Quality Assurance Group rated quality at entry satisfactory in seven of the nine areas it assessed and moderately satisfactory in two, the resettlement process and the estimation of motorised traffic growth. The review also says the project had no road safety indicator at all. All these figures are the lender's own, and the Evaluation Group sits inside the World Bank Group, so none of them is a check from outside it.
wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.why: ICRR13574 is the only evaluative document: a query to the World Bank documents API for P069852 returns 18 documents, among them the conformed Loan and Project Agreements for L4727, the appraisal document, resettlement plans and this review, and no Implementation Completion and Results Report, so the single-document weakness stands. Corrections: the review's road-safety sentence reads 'In Wuchang district alone the number of fatalities (mostly pedestrians and cyclists) was halved during the course of the project from 23 in 2004 to 65 in 2009', which contradicts itself, so the sentence and both figures are removed and nothing is claimed about road deaths; the review's own M&E section says there was no road safety indicator. The same pair of figures, US$398.20m and US$1,110.66m, is labelled project cost in the data sheet and borrower contribution in section 2d, and the US$713 million rise is the difference between them, so the labels are reported as printed rather than treated as two separate facts. Travel times are now in the review's own relative terms. Added from section 9: the Wuhan Public Transport Group Company failed to implement 13 of 37 public transport subprojects. ERR coverage 93 per cent at appraisal and 94 per cent at the ICR, from the rate table.

tedap-ukonga-mzinga-wayleaves.whole: By the completion report's count the project built or rehabilitated 184.4 kilometres of distribution line against a target of 282 kilometres set at the 2015 restructuring, and 37.1 kilometres of transmission line against 57.1, the row's comment putting the transmission figure at about 37.4 kilometres: 13 kilometres of the Ubungo to Kurasini section could not be built because the national roads agency's Mandela Road expansion took the wayleave, and the 1.3 kilometres at Mzinga Creek was still being procured and installed at closing, with completion expected on 31 March 2018. The borrower's own section of the report says the 132 kV southern ring circuit planned for Dar es Salaam, running from the Factory Zone III substation through Factory Zone II, Mbagala and Kurasini to Ubungo, was removed from the project's scope for that reason, so the ring circuit could not be realised in the time available. End-user voltage reached 220 volts against a target of 218 from a baseline of 190; losses in the project area fell from 28 per cent to 16.44 against a target of 21; collection efficiency rose from 70 per cent to 94 against a target of 95; 25.45 MW of grid-connected small power generation was installed against 17 MW at appraisal and a revised 25 MW; 85,000 prepaid meters were installed against a target of 60,000; and 30,933 households were connected under the on-grid component against a revised target of 25,000. On the off-grid side the rural energy agency concluded 65 subproject transactions against a revised target of 10, standard power purchase agreements covered 58.3 MW of installed capacity against a revised 20 MW, rural household connections reached 71,966 against a target of 40,000, 144,622 households were connected under that component against a revised target of 110,000, which the report converts to 694,189 people at 4.8 people a household, and 206,149 direct beneficiaries were recorded against 20,000 at appraisal and a revised 114,000. Two rows fell short: customer satisfaction at the utility was 62 per cent against a target of 75, a gap the report calls 13 percentage points, and community connections - dispensaries, health centres, secondary schools, staff houses, police posts and public lighting - came to 996 against 800 at appraisal and a revised 1,200. Activities cancelled: the customer management system with its trouble and resource management modules, and the centralised call centre and high-value customer cell, both over budget overruns, with the first later taken into another Bank project; and in 2009 the procurement of four distribution packages, after the Bank objected to shortcomings in the bidding and its settlement with Siemens AG required the preferred bidder in three of the four packages to withdraw. The report puts the project's economic rate of return at 13 per cent with a net present value of TZS 24 billion (US$19 million) at a 10 per cent discount rate, covering 99 per cent of project cost, with the grid component at 17 per cent against 31 per cent at appraisal; one of the two mini-grids analysed returned minus 9 per cent, and photovoltaic installations in institutions returned minus 13 per cent with a net present value of minus US$2 million, against 21 per cent and US$300,000 at appraisal. No rate of return for the project as a whole was given at appraisal, and the report sets out why it includes no financial analysis. Both the report and the Evaluation Group's review rate efficiency Modest and the outcome Moderately Satisfactory on a split rating. Spending came to US$143.67 million against US$171.88 million at appraisal, with no borrower contribution, and the project closed five and a half years after its original date. All these figures are the lender's own; no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
tedap-ukonga-mzinga-wayleaves.why: Checked against ICR00004395 (Annex 1 row by row, paragraphs 24-27, 41-42, 67-71 and Table 5, paragraph 127, the borrower's section at page 90) and ICRR in full. Corrections: the Component A connection row is labelled persons but its comment reads 'The target of 25,000 households was exceeded by 24 percent and reached 30,933', and the Component B row of the same name carries households (144,622) with the conversion to 694,189 people, so 30,933 is households; the southern ring circuit statement is in the borrower's own 'Next Steps' section of the report, not the Bank's text; the community connections target was raised from 800 to 1,200; the transmission row's comment gives 37.4 km where the row gives 37.1; paragraph 71 carries the negative return on photovoltaic installations in institutions, which was missing; paragraph 127 adds the Siemens settlement behind the 2009 cancellation. Paragraph 68 states that the appraisal document gave no project-wide ENPV or EIRR, and paragraph 67 explains why no financial analysis is included.

ctb-kwabenya-stone-crackers.whole: In Ghana the project built the 330 kV Aboadze to Tema transmission line with its terminal substations, which the completion report says were commissioned in late 2009; upgraded switchgear and electromechanical equipment at the Aboadze switchyard and the Volta switching system, including circuit breakers, disconnect switches and protection and control facilities; installed telecommunication equipment for the third bulk supply point at the Accra East and Achimota substations; and upgraded the supervisory control and data acquisition and energy management systems, with the Akosombo and Kpong generating station reinforcements and the control centre completed by June 2013. A dam safety assessment and an emergency preparedness plan for the Akosombo, Kpong and Nangbeto stations were delivered, and power sector monitoring data for the regional member states were collected and disseminated. In Benin and Togo the new dispatching centre at the bi-national utility's headquarters and the backup centre in Cotonou were completed and operating at closing, and the dispatch modernisation, rehabilitation and emergency plan studies and a draft procedures manual were finished. Apart from those emergency plans and the monitoring data, every indicator was recorded at its baseline value or at nil, because the regional project was not commissioned by the closing date: no electricity was traded over the project's infrastructure, power losses along the interconnection links stayed at 6, 4, 8 and 4 per cent for the four utilities against a 2 per cent target for each, and the targets for outage reduction, detection and response time, delivered capacity and reactive power are all recorded as not achieved. Construction along the 330 kV line in Benin was unfinished when the Bank closed the financing of that activity on 30 June 2016, the report saying the Bank no longer had the resources for it and putting the remaining works at US$5 million to US$6 million, beyond the bi-national utility's own means; the cooperation agreement for the backbone is recorded as not in place. The Volta River Authority's control centre study was not completed and its training centre was not set up. At appraisal the Evaluation Group's review gives economic rates of return of 16 per cent for Ghana and 35 per cent for Benin on components accounting for 85 and 87 per cent of the appraisal estimates, with a net present value of US$64 million at a 10 per cent discount rate. At completion only the Ghana investments could be analysed, and the line was loaded at about 15 per cent of its 400 MW nominal capacity: the report's scenario at a 20 per cent load factor gives a benefit-cost ratio of 0.4 and a rate of return of 0.3 per cent, and a ratio above 1 needs the load factor at about 75 per cent. Gas through the West African Gas Pipeline did not materialise, so there was limited production to send over the line at its design capacity, and the aluminium smelter demand assumed at the Tema end did not materialise either. Both the report and the review rate efficiency Negligible and the outcome Unsatisfactory, and the report puts the risk to the development outcome High. All these figures are the lender's own; no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
ctb-kwabenya-stone-crackers.why: Checked against ICR00004338 (section F row by row - three PDO and nine intermediate indicators - paragraphs 30, 55-57 and Annex 3) and the review's sections 4 and 5 in full. Corrections: two intermediate rows, the emergency preparedness plans (deployed 20 December 2013) and the power sector monitoring data (completed 14 April 2016), were fully achieved, so 'every outcome indicator' is now qualified; Annex 3 gives the three scenarios behind the summary statement, of which Scenario 1 (20 per cent load factor, US$0.01 per kWh differential) yields a benefit-cost ratio of 0.4 and an EIRR of 0.3 per cent and Scenario 2 (75 per cent) a ratio of 1.14, which replaces the vaguer 'below 12 per cent'; Annex 3 paragraph 4 adds that the Volta Aluminium Company load assumed at appraisal did not materialise; the review's paragraph before its efficiency section gives US$5-6 million as the cost of the remaining Benin works, beyond CEB's internal financing capability. The review's own rate table prints 86.00 as the appraisal point value with 23.00 as coverage, which matches nothing in either document's text, and its sentence 'the global NPV was 23%' is garbled; neither is used.

wapp-apl3-zagtouli-bolgatanga-deaths.whole: The project built the 225 kV line from Bolgatanga in Ghana to the Zagtouli substation at Ouagadougou: 188 kilometres, 171 in Burkina Faso and 17 in Ghana, against 210 kilometres planned at appraisal, the Ghana length having fallen from 39 kilometres when the end-of-line substation moved from Bolgatanga I to Bolgatanga II, with 22 kilometres of the Burkina Faso section built as double circuit. It also built a 330/225/161 kV substation at Bolgatanga, extended the 225/90 kV Zagtouli substation, built a new 90/33 kV substation in Burkina Faso, installed telecommunications, supervisory control and energy management systems, and installed a 330/161 kV transformer at Aboadze; it funded strengthened management of the Kabore Tambi National Park and pre-investment studies for the proposed 330 kV Dawa to Bolgatanga line in place of the 161 kV Atebubu to Tamale line studied at appraisal. Twenty-five villages along the right of way were electrified, 14 from the existing 33 kV network and 11 from shield wires on the new line, rather than from the new line itself as first conceived. Every indicator was met or exceeded by the completion report's count: the weighted average annual cost of electricity supply in Burkina Faso fell from US$0.26 to US$0.20 a kilowatt-hour against a target of US$0.25; the annual duration of outages from generation shortfall and load shedding fell from 130 hours to 8, its target; the interconnection line ran 8,497 hours in the year against a target of 7,884; exports from Ghana to Burkina Faso reached 222 GWh against a target of 158; 3,474 rural households along the right of way were connected against a target of 3,400; 20,844 people were counted as direct beneficiaries against 20,400, 55 per cent of them women, the target; and 82 staff were trained in live network operation and maintenance against 81. The Evaluation Group's 2022 assessment of the project, drawing on the Burkina Faso utility's figures, reports exports rising to 1,177 GWh in 2022, 48 per cent of the country's grid electricity supply, and outages down from 58 minutes a year in 2018 to 33 minutes; it says sustaining the lower cost is uncertain because it turns on surplus power in Ghana, oil prices, fuel transport costs, demand growth and the security situation. The report puts the economic rate of return at 29.7 per cent at completion against 32.6 per cent at appraisal, with a net present value of US$230 million at a 10 per cent discount rate against US$284 million, over 95 per cent of project cost, and the financial return at 29.6 per cent for Burkina Faso's utility against 37 per cent at appraisal and 13.47 per cent for Ghana's against 12.2 per cent; incremental transmission losses were 2.3 per cent against 5 per cent assumed at appraisal, and 1.13 per cent measured in 2018, when the line had run half a year. Both the report and the Evaluation Group's review rate efficiency Substantial and the outcome Satisfactory, and both rate overall Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory. The project took 18 months from approval to effectiveness because of cross-conditions among the three financiers, and the Bank withdrew its money from the line itself and put it into the Bolgatanga substation, with the French Development Agency moving the other way, to get past disagreements over joint procurement. The completion report's financing table records nothing at completion from the French Development Agency, the European Investment Bank or the two borrowers, against US$32.3 million, US$30.9 million and US$5.9 million planned at approval, and a total actual cost of US$36.3 million against US$111 million at approval. All these figures are the lender's own, from its completion report and the Evaluation Group's review and later assessment of it; the Group sits inside the World Bank Group, and no check from outside it was found.
wapp-apl3-zagtouli-bolgatanga-deaths.why: Checked against ICR00004695 (Annex 1 all nine rows, key outputs, paragraphs 19-24 with Table 5, paragraphs 43-48 with Table 8, the financing table), ICRR and PPAR 187586. Corrections: paragraph 22 records the line falling from 210 km (171 in Burkina Faso, 39 in Ghana) to 188 km (171 and 17) with the substation moved from Bolgatanga I to Bolgatanga II, so 210 km is the appraisal figure and not what was built; the same paragraph gives the switch of pre-investment studies to the Dawa-Bolgatanga line and the village electrification through existing 33 kV lines and shield wires instead of full electrification from the new line, with Table 5 giving 14 and 11 villages. On the 2022 export figure the assessment prints 1,777 GWh once, in a page-11 summary box, against 1,177 GWh in its overview, in paragraph 3.4 and in Table 3.1, where 1,177 of 2,457 GWh is the 48 per cent share sourced to SONABEL 2023; the single higher figure is a misprint that the document's own table settles, so only 1,177 is given. Outages fell from 58 minutes in 2018 to 33 in 2022 (paragraph 3.5 area, page 13).

benin-iame-transmission-compensation.whole: The project built 284.7 kilometres of 161 kV transmission line against a target of 310 - the 30 kilometre Sakete to Tanzoun line and the 254.7 kilometre Onigbolo to Parakou line, whose length fell from an estimated 280 kilometres when the design and right of way were finalised, which is why the completion report records that row as met - and the report records the Onigbolo to Parakou line completed in November 2018 and the transmission network meeting the N-1 reliability criterion, its target. It rehabilitated and reinforced the distribution networks of Cotonou, Porto-Novo, Sakete, Bohicon, Allada, Parakou and Natitingou, after which measurement campaigns found voltage fluctuation above 7 per cent eliminated in those cities; installed 45,000 prepayment meters and 350,000 compact fluorescent bulbs, both targets; developed and applied efficiency standards for bulbs and air conditioners; brought 300,000 hectares of the Moyen Oueme protected area under forest management plans with rural wood markets installed; and trained 1,150 people in improved carbonisation and logging techniques against a target of 450. People with electricity through household connections reached 3,880,116 against a target of 3,900,000, which the report calls almost achieved, on 210,735 new subscribers between 2009 and 2017 plus 7,168 connections in the first quarter of 2018; direct beneficiaries were put at 2,214,235 against a target of 200,000 in the framework row, whose own comment gives 2,311,661. Three rows fell short. Losses on Benin's transmission network were 67.6 GWh at completion against a target of 24 GWh and a baseline of 51 GWh; the report gives the same years as a loss rate falling from 5.44 per cent in 2009 to 4.8 per cent in 2018 on a flow that grew from 937 to 1,409 GWh, and attributes the 2017 rise to poor supply voltage from Nigeria and to the Bohicon to Onigbolo line being out of service while the Sakete to Onigbolo line was built. Losses in the project area were 23.09 per cent against a target of 20 and a baseline of 22, the non-technical part 13.09 per cent against 10, which the report says the project was not designed to address. And the energy efficiency component's savings came to 6.61 MW of peak load and 12.06 GWh against targets of 9.7 MW and 14 GWh, because 40-watt bulbs were replaced as well as the 60-watt bulbs assumed. None of the four planned stand-alone rural generation systems was built: after the rural electrification concession study was delayed, the money was moved at the 2013 restructuring to on-grid electrification of new localities, where 3,150 people were connected against a target of 3,000. The report's recalculated economic rates of return are 36 per cent for the transmission lines against 22 per cent at appraisal, 40 per cent for distribution against 16 per cent, and 92 per cent for energy efficiency against 53 per cent, at a 10 per cent discount rate, and it notes the transmission figures use the appraisal assumptions because the line was finished just before closing and no data on its effect existed; the Evaluation Group's review records an appraisal rate of 20 per cent covering 55 per cent of project cost and no recalculated rate in its own table. Both the report and the review rate efficiency Modest and the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, on a project that closed three and a half years after its original date. The appraisal's financial projections for the two utilities proved highly inaccurate, the report says, both companies' finances having worsened significantly since 2010 with public-sector non-payment and persistent losses, and no financial analysis was done at completion. The credit was cut to US$54.38 million and US$52.78 million was disbursed. All these figures are the lender's own; no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
benin-iame-transmission-compensation.why: Checked against the completion report for P110075 (Annex 1 row by row, paragraphs 71-78 with Tables 5 and 6, the data sheet) and ICRR section 5 with its rate table. Corrections: the transmission-line row's comment reads 'This target is met' even though 284.7 km is below the 310 km target, which is now stated; the direct-beneficiaries row's comment gives 2,311,661 against the row's 2,214,235, so both are given; the Component B3 row (3,150 people connected against 3,000) is added, since the money for the cancelled stand-alone systems went there. All other rows verified, including the three short rows already present.

pakistan-edtip-crop-compensation.whole: The completion report records 75 of 114 planned distribution subprojects completed, 65 per cent, and 73 per cent of the revised loan amount disbursed. Of the subprojects planned, 11 of 13 were completed at the Hyderabad distribution company, 25 of 31 at Islamabad, 8 of 31 at Lahore - where only 10 were ever awarded - and 31 of 39 at Multan, with grid stations at Bahter More, Gangal, Saggian, Mominpura and D G Khan unfinished at closing and expected by September 2014. In the transmission component the new 220 kV grid station at Kassowal was about 79 per cent complete, some 20 months past its scheduled date and expected in December 2014, with about US$6 million of the cost falling beyond closing on the national transmission company; its transmission line was complete. Because Kassowal was unfinished, loading at the Yousufwala and Vehari grid stations stayed at 100 per cent against targets of 77 and 74 per cent. Losses fell at two companies and rose at two: Islamabad's annual transmission and distribution losses came to 8.6 per cent from a baseline of 12.2, beating both the appraisal target of 11.4 and the revised 9.55; Multan's 17.6 per cent beat a revised 18.0 but not the appraisal 17.4, and stayed above the regulator's 15 per cent for that year; Hyderabad's 33.2 per cent was worse than a revised target of 32.2 and far above the regulator's 24.9 per cent; and Lahore's 13.2 per cent was worse than its own 12.8 baseline and worse than a target revised upwards to 12.1. Electricity handled met revised targets at Islamabad, 8,830 GWh against 8,784 after a cut from 11,640, and at Multan, 13,274 against 12,830 after a cut from 14,398, and missed them at Hyderabad, 9,356 against 9,683, and Lahore, 16,458 against 18,126, which the report attributes to the country's supply shortfall. Collection as a share of billing fell short at three companies - Islamabad 90.0 per cent against a revised 95.9, Hyderabad 67.6 against a revised 73.5, Multan 93.2 against 99.5 - the report noting non-payment by public-sector consumers, collection from private consumers close to 100 per cent, and that this indicator is not related to the project's works. The tariff differential subsidy, which measures the cost not recovered from consumer revenues, came in far above its revised target at three of the four companies: PKR 34,207 million against 6,969 million at Islamabad, 28,681 against 19,302 at Hyderabad and 19,786 against 14,177 at Lahore, which the report puts down to higher power purchase costs not passed on to consumers. Revised targets for line tripping were missed at Islamabad, Hyderabad and Lahore, with interruptions over 20 minutes higher than the baseline at Hyderabad. Training targets were met on a cumulative basis, with 936 staff trained at Islamabad, 320 at Hyderabad, 667 at Lahore and 855 at Multan between 2007 and 2013. Dropped at the June 2012 restructuring: distribution works worth about US$38.28 million held not to be urgently needed, technical assistance worth about US$8.72 million, and the whole energy efficiency component, about US$15 million, on which nothing was spent; US$62 million of the loan, a quarter of it, was cancelled then and about US$2 million more in February 2014. A further US$32 million of contracts were never awarded, among them two new grid stations in Lahore and 40 MVA power transformers that the Lahore company's board later scrapped, and a distribution transformer contract in Multan stopped by a High Court stay order; contracts worth about US$56 million were not completed by the closing date, and about US$15 million of spending fell beyond it, to be met by the utilities themselves. Of the US$256.70 million of Bank financing at appraisal, revised to US$192.61 million, US$140.60 million was disbursed, and total project cost came to US$159.59 million against US$309.86 million at appraisal, with the borrower providing US$18.98 million of the US$53.16 million planned. The report puts the economic rate of return at 47 per cent at completion against 22 per cent at appraisal, covering 97 and 90 per cent of project cost, with the loss reduction works returning most of the gain because power purchase costs had more than tripled since appraisal. The Evaluation Group's review rates efficiency Substantial and both documents rate the overall outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, the report saying the project missed 50 per cent of its targets and rating Bank and borrower performance Unsatisfactory. All these figures are the lender's own; no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
pakistan-edtip-crop-compensation.why: Checked against ICR3137 (section F, all 18 PDO rows and all 20 intermediate rows, Tables 2.1 and 2.2, Annex 1, sections 3.3-3.4) and ICRR14881 in full. Corrections: the report's section 3.3 Efficiency carries no rating line, and the only Substantial rating near it is section 4's risk to development outcome, so the efficiency rating is attributed to the review alone, which states it in its section 6; the shortfall test added the tariff differential subsidy rows for three companies and the line-tripping rows, both families of adverse intermediate rows; '73 per cent disbursed' is 73 per cent of the revised loan (US$140.60m of US$192.61m, 55 per cent of the US$256.70m at appraisal), so the financing figures are given; Table 2.1 shows Lahore awarded only 10 of its 31 subprojects; the US$15 million of spending beyond the closing date to be funded by the utilities is from the Component A section; the energy efficiency component shows nil actual spending in Annex 1.

kiidp-kampala-roads-compensation.whole: The completion report records that the project expanded and lined 3.6 kilometres of the Lubigi primary drainage channel, its target, and upgraded gravel roads to bitumen standard on 11.81 kilometres of the about 14.42 kilometres planned at approval, of which 8.73 kilometres was fully complete and open at closing against a target revised to 12.89 kilometres, the rest being finished by the city council itself by the end of May 2014. It developed six acres of land next to the existing landfill, trained 76 staff in contract management and revenue collection, bought 25 vehicles along with information technology and records management equipment, extended the council's network to division offices, carried out its financial recovery plan, completed a strategic planning process and five public consultations, and updated the Kampala Physical Development Plan. The city council's stock of overdue liabilities fell from UGX 8 billion to zero against an original target of UGX 3 billion and a revised UGX 0.5 billion, though the report adds that UGX 2.6 billion was still recorded as a liability with no supporting documents for the claims and was to be written off after verification. Own-source revenue rose from UGX 22 billion in 2005/06 to UGX 55.71 billion in 2012/13, against an original target of UGX 30 billion and a revised UGX 33.5 billion, and the report puts its average annual growth at 12.2 per cent during the project against 6.4 per cent in the seven years before it. The share of own-source revenue spent on service delivery reached 32.7 per cent against 10 per cent at the start, an original target of 30 per cent and a revised 34. Building permit approval fell from a year in 2006 to two months, the share of property owners issued rate demand notes rose from 30 per cent in 2006 to 100 per cent in 2013, traffic on the upgraded roads grew 31 per cent against a revised target of 20 per cent on an indicator added at restructuring, and the number of people affected by floods along the Lubigi channel fell from 8,800 to none. Public satisfaction, the fourth outcome indicator, was not met on any of its three measures: roads 29 per cent against a target of 50, drainage 22 per cent against 31 and solid waste 46 per cent against 60, and the report notes that the figures come from citizens report card surveys covering services across Kampala rather than the project's own works. Works were dropped at the first restructuring, in December 2010: the secondary drainage channels, 4 kilometres of them, and four tertiary drainage black spots, both recorded at zero; the area traffic management works; the landfill gas collection and flaring system; the maintenance of about 26 kilometres of tarmac roads, recorded as zero against 374.07 kilometres of bitumen roads to be improved, after a national road fund took over road maintenance; and the infrastructure for the Kibuli and Kawempe markets. A human resources management system was dropped when a national payroll system was rolled out, and a complaints management system, customer care desks, a client charter and a perceptions survey were not implemented. The report says the money was moved to cover resettlement costs under the resettlement action plan, extended consultancies and higher operating costs, the government's own contribution having fallen short. The report puts the economic rate of return on the road works at 29.8 per cent at completion against 32 per cent at appraisal: three of the five roads returned more than the 12 per cent discount rate, while Kimera returned 7.9 per cent with a net present value of minus US$0.378 million and Soweto 9.6 per cent with minus US$0.256 million, which the report attributes to actual construction costs per kilometre more than twice the estimate. The return on the Lubigi channel was 17.5 per cent at completion, against 14.0 per cent at appraisal in the report's table and 16.8 per cent in the Evaluation Group's review. The report rates efficiency Satisfactory and the outcome Moderately Satisfactory; the review rates efficiency Substantial and the outcome Satisfactory. On the institutional side the report sets US$1.62 million of spending against a UGX 33.71 billion rise in own-source revenue and calls the efficiency potentially very high, while the review says the efficiency of that spending cannot be assessed, for want of information on what the council itself spent to raise its revenue and of any benchmark for an efficient revenue collection system. The project cost US$35.64 million against US$37.10 million at appraisal, with US$33.58 million of the US$33.6 million credit disbursed and US$2.06 million of the US$3.5 million expected from the government provided, and the closing date was extended twice, by three years in total. All these figures are the lender's own; no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
kiidp-kampala-roads-compensation.why: The completion report for this project is published and has been added to the cache: ICR00002916, 27 June 2014, found through the World Bank documents API for P078382 and read in full for section F, paragraphs 25-28, 71-83 and Annexes 1 and 3. The paragraph is rewritten on it, so this case no longer rests on the review alone. Corrections to the earlier text: the public satisfaction indicator was missed on all three measures (roads 29 against 50, drainage 22 against 31, solid waste 46 against 60) and was omitted; the gravel-roads row gives 8.73 km fully complete against a revised 12.89 km, with 11.81 km supported in total; the overdue-liabilities row's comment records UGX 2.6 billion of unsupported claims still outstanding; the service-delivery share (32.7 against a revised 34) and the dropped bitumen-maintenance indicator (0 against 374.07 km) were missing, as were the flood and traffic indicators; the report's table gives the Lubigi appraisal return as 14.0 per cent where the review gives 16.8, so both are named; the report rates efficiency Satisfactory and the outcome Moderately Satisfactory against the review's Substantial and Satisfactory, a ratings disagreement that the single-document version could not show; the per-road figures and the cost reason come from the report's own table; paragraph 26 explains the reallocation to resettlement costs and gives the government's contribution falling to US$1.55 million in the revised plan, against US$2.06 million actually spent in Annex 1, which is the figure used. Annex 2's output tables also record the human resources management system dropped at restructuring and four communication activities not implemented, which are included.

tanzania-tscp-compensation-delays.whole: By the completion report's count the project paved or rebuilt 253.6 kilometres of non-rural road against 140 at appraisal and a target raised to 220, built or rehabilitated 42.02 kilometres of stand-alone drains against 15 and a revised 31, built or rehabilitated 277 waste collection points against 231 and a revised 255, built or improved seven sanitary landfills with 17 cells against five and a revised seven, built or improved 11 bus, daladala and lorry stands with room for 1,471 vehicles against six stands and 600 vehicles at appraisal and a revised ten and 1,100, and delivered 29 gender-sensitive features, among them paved walkways, raised humps near schools, footbridges and a playground, against a target of 17 set at restructuring. 1,890,687 people were counted as direct beneficiaries against 952,806 at appraisal and a revised 1,741,000, and 1,278,053 as having access to improved bus stations, terminals or lorry stands against 543,721 and a revised 1,266,200. Waste reaching landfills rose from 28 per cent of the waste generated to 86 per cent, against 58 per cent at appraisal and a target cut to 40 per cent because the first landfill began operating in the third quarter of 2016 rather than 2013. Own-source revenue in the eight local authorities rose 457 per cent over the 2010 base year against 45 per cent at appraisal and a revised 100 per cent, which the report attributes partly to the cities' rapid growth and to plot sales, a major revenue source, counting inside that revenue. Spending on operation and maintenance reached 28 per cent of municipal expenditure against 16 per cent at appraisal and a revised 20; fees and charges covered 84 per cent of solid waste operating costs against 12 per cent at appraisal and a revised 25, and 95 per cent of bus and lorry stand costs against 65 and a revised 80 - though the report's financial analysis says solid waste charges and fees do not cover operating costs, which it calls a risk to the sustainability of the facilities. Seven local authorities had up-to-date strategic urban development plans and general planning schemes, both targets met, and all project-related grievances were recorded as addressed. Four indicators were dropped: up-to-date property valuations and property tax collected, after responsibility for valuation, billing and collection moved to the Tanzania Revenue Authority from 1 July 2016, and roads in good or fair condition and people with access to an all-season road, as measures the project did not control. Institutional strengthening work on urban planning systems, geographic information systems and own-source revenue was dropped after delays in mobilisation and the pandemic and taken up by a follow-on project, and solid waste and geographic information equipment contracts were ended by mutual agreement with suppliers who could not produce in time. The report's economic analysis of a sample of works puts the rate of return at 40 per cent with a net present value of US$65 million - 48 per cent for urban roads, 32 per cent for the Arusha landfill, 33 per cent for the Duga drainage, 13 per cent for the Tanga bus station and 12 per cent for solid waste in Tanga - against 22 per cent at appraisal over 94 per cent of project cost in the Evaluation Group's table, and says actual investment costs at appraisal prices were 10 per cent below expectations and benefits three times costs. Both the report and the review rate efficiency Substantial and the outcome Satisfactory. The project ran on three credits totalling US$343 million, of which US$340.37 million was disbursed; the US$12.5 million expected from the Danish government at approval is recorded as nothing at completion, and total cost came to US$340.37 million against US$355.5 million at appraisal. All these figures are the lender's own; no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
tanzania-tscp-compensation-delays.why: Checked against ICR00005449 (Annex 1 row by row, paragraphs 16 and 30-36, footnote 9, the outcomes chapter and the financing table) and ICRR with its rate table. Every framework row is met or exceeded, so the shortfall test found nothing to add; the counter-figure on solid waste cost recovery against the financial analysis in paragraph 35 is kept. agara-zemo-osiauri-e60-agarebi.whole: The project built 12 kilometres of two-lane dual carriageway from Agara to Zemo Osiauri, its target, maintained 67 kilometres of the E60 between Natakhtari and Ruisi under a multi-year contract, and put road safety measures and access roads on 100 kilometres of the E60 between Natakhtari and Ruisi and between Agara and Chumateleti, all recorded as delivered. Transit time from Agara to Kashuri fell from 10 minutes to 7, its target; vehicle operating costs fell from US$0.20 to US$0.18 a kilometre for cars and from US$0.76 to US$0.72 for trucks, both targets; and the road fatality rate on the Tbilisi to Senaki section of the corridor fell from 11.6 to 3.03 deaths per 100 million vehicle-kilometres against a target of 8.5 - a stretch of about 275 kilometres, which the Evaluation Group's review notes is far longer than the 12 kilometres built or the 111 kilometres given safety works, so that earlier work on policing and public awareness also bears on it. A road sector strategy taking in social and gender dimensions was adopted, as were an updated road safety strategy and action plan and a roadmap for intelligent transport systems, and the feasibility study from Zemo to Argveta and the detailed engineering design from Zemo Osiauri to Chumateleti were completed. Two rows were not delivered: the training needs assessments and manpower development plans for the Roads Department and for the ministry, replaced by a gap analysis of which one deliverable was finished under this loan and the rest moved to a follow-on project, which is part of why the review rates the institutional strengthening objective Modest. The asset value of the East-West Highway corridor from Tbilisi to Sarpi rose by GEL 1,599 million against a target the completion report's framework gives as GEL 2,200 million and the review gives as GEL 2,300 million, about 70 per cent of it; the review attributes the gap to the delayed completion of the Samtredia to Grigoleti section financed by the European Investment Bank and to the upgrading of the Zemo Osiauri to Chumateleti Lot 2 section, whose contract was terminated in December 2018 and which was being tendered again under another project, and says this asset value is the cumulative book value of recent investments rather than a measure of economic benefit or one that accounts for depreciation. The report puts the economic rate of return at 19.9 per cent at completion against 17.5 per cent at appraisal, with a net present value at a 12 per cent discount rate that its text gives as US$37.7 million and its own table as US$37.3 million, against US$26.7 million at appraisal, and says the higher result comes mainly from reduced project costs and higher traffic than appraisal assumed, with the extension of the closing date having no effect because the civil works contract finished on time. The report rates efficiency High; the review rates it Substantial, on the road works being 56 per cent of the project as completed against 62 per cent covered at appraisal, a closing date two years late and some analytical work deferred. All these figures are the lender's own; no check from outside the World Bank Group was found.
